title: The Order in Which Savings Candidates Are Tried for a Personal Checking Protection Source
content:
Two cases change the order in which the owner's savings accounts held under Savings & Money Market Accounts are tried as the protection source for a Personal Checking account.

- Where the owner has made at least 6 card payments in the last twelve months under Personal Credit Cards **and** the owner's premier money market balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00, the premier money market account is tried first and the statement savings account second.
- Where the case above does not apply **and** either the owner holds any statement savings balance at all **or** the owner's certificate principal held under Certificates of Deposit is above zero, whichever of the two carries the greater usable cover is tried first.
- Where neither case applies, neither of those orders is used.

**Worked orders on hypothetical inputs.** An owner holds a statement savings account whose usable cover is 3000.00 and a premier money market account whose usable cover is 8000.00, against a requirement of 1500.00.

| Owner's position | Order tried | Source named |
|---|---|---|
| 7 card payments, premier money market balance of 9000.00 | Premier money market account, then statement savings | The premier money market account |
| 2 card payments, statement savings balance of 6000.00 | The greater usable cover first, so the premier money market account | The premier money market account |
| 2 card payments, no statement savings balance, certificate principal of 700.00 | The greater usable cover first | The premier money market account |
| 2 card payments, no statement savings balance, no certificate principal | Neither order is used |  |

The order matters only where more than one candidate reaches the requirement, since the first candidate that reaches it is the one named. Equality satisfies each threshold, so exactly 6 card payments with a premier money market balance of exactly 5000.00 reaches the first case.
